abuse-reports-api: Cloudflare abuse reports: submit a new abuse report, and list or view reports filed against the account's domains and content, as well as reports the account submitted. Also covers mitigations applied to a report, emails sent to customers or submitters, checking whether a report can be appealed, and requesting mitigation review or an appeal.
accounts-applications: Cloudflare account applications, the named apps that rules can match on: list the applications available to an account (Cloudflare-provided and custom), get one by ID, create custom applications with a category and network matchers, update matchers (creates a new version), delete them, and look up application names mentioned in a rule sentence.
accounts-billing: Cloudflare account billing: view billing history, download receipt PDFs, and check credit balance. Also covers unpaid invoices and bad debt, paying an invoice (including SCA verification), and payment methods (add via Stripe setup intent, list, update, delete, set default). Turn PDF invoice generation on or off.
accounts-core: Cloudflare accounts: create, list, view, rename, move into an organization, and delete accounts; see which organizations contain an account; edit the business profile (name, email, phone, address); check feature entitlements; browse audit logs and change history; application categories; Image Resizing configurations and Unique Transformations billing settings.
accounts-members: Cloudflare account members: add a user to an account, list all members, view one member's details, change a member's settings (such as roles), and remove a member from the account.
accounts-subscriptions: Cloudflare account and zone subscriptions (paid plans): list subscriptions or fetch one by ID, create, update or delete a subscription, record and read the reason for a cancellation, and cancel a pending delayed downgrade.
accounts-tokens: Cloudflare account-owned API tokens (tokens owned by the account rather than a user): create, list, inspect, update and delete tokens, roll a token's secret, verify that a token works, and look up the available permission groups to grant when scoping a token.
acm-api: Cloudflare Advanced Certificate Manager for a zone: upload, list, inspect and delete root CA certificates in the Custom Origin Trust Store so origins signed by a private CA are trusted, and view, enable, configure or disable Total TLS, which issues certificates for hostnames automatically.
addressing-address-maps: Cloudflare Address Maps (addressing): create, list, view, edit and delete address maps (a map must be disabled before deletion), and manage their members. Add or remove IPs from owned prefixes, zones, and other accounts, singly or in bulk.
addressing-core: Cloudflare Address Space for Bring-Your-Own-IP (BYOIP): upload, list and download LOA (Letter of Authorization) PDF documents, list the account's IP address leases, and list the Cloudflare services, with their service IDs, that an onboarded IP prefix can be bound to.
addressing-prefixes: Cloudflare Address Space (BYOIP) IP prefixes: add, list, edit the description of, validate (IRR, RPKI, ownership) and delete prefixes; advertise or withdraw BGP prefixes for specific subnets; delegate a prefix to other accounts; and bind prefix CIDRs to Cloudflare services.
addressing-regional-hostnames: Cloudflare Regional Services hostnames: restrict where HTTPS traffic for a zone's hostname is decrypted and served by pinning it to data centers in a chosen region (data localization). List available regions, and create, list, inspect, change the region of, or delete regional hostnames.
agent-memory-api: Cloudflare Agent Memory, long-term memory for AI agents: create, list and delete namespaces and profiles, ingest conversations to extract facts, events, instructions and tasks, store a single memory directly, recall relevant memories as a synthesized answer, list, get or delete memories, delete a session, and generate a prompt-ready profile summary.
ai-api: Cloudflare Workers AI: run models for inference (by model name in the URL or in the request body), find models by name, author, or task type, and get a model's input/output schema. Also covers fine-tuning (upload training data, create, list, delete, download assets, public fine-tunes), converting files to Markdown, and web search via AI Gateway.
ai-audit-api: Cloudflare AI Audit: fetch and parse a site's robots.txt, for one zone or subdomain, or for many domains in a zone at once. Returns the user-agent rules (such as which AI crawlers are allowed or blocked), content signals, and sitemaps, keyed by hostname.
ai-gateway-custom-domains: Cloudflare AI Gateway custom domains: attach your own hostname to a gateway, get the CNAME target to point DNS at, list the domains on a gateway, check a domain's status, certificate and validation state, and remove a domain along with its custom hostname.
ai-gateway-custom-providers: Cloudflare AI Gateway custom providers: register your own AI model endpoint by HTTPS base URL so gateway requests can route to it as `custom-{slug}`. Create, list, inspect, update (base URL, custom headers) and delete providers; deleting one also removes its pricing rules.
ai-gateway-datasets: AI Gateway datasets: create, list, inspect, update (name, log filters, enabled state) and delete datasets that select gateway logs matching filters for use in evaluations. Datasets and evaluations are deprecated and unavailable to new accounts.
ai-gateway-dynamic-routing: Cloudflare AI Gateway dynamic routing: create, list, inspect, rename and delete dynamic routes that clients call as `dynamic/{name}` in place of a model name. Save new versions of a route's routing elements, view versions, deploy a version to serve traffic, roll back to an earlier one, and see deployment history.
ai-gateway-evaluations: AI Gateway evaluations: create an evaluation that scores the logs in a dataset with chosen evaluator types, list the evaluations run on a gateway, retrieve one with its results, and delete one. Evaluations and datasets are deprecated and unavailable to new accounts.
ai-gateway-gateways: Cloudflare AI Gateway: create, list, update and delete gateways with caching, rate limiting, logging and authentication settings, and get a gateway's endpoint URL. Also manage the upstream AI provider API keys stored for a gateway (masked on read), and list evaluator types (evaluations are deprecated).
ai-gateway-logs: Cloudflare AI Gateway request logs: list and filter logged AI requests with pagination, view details of a single log entry, fetch its original request payload and its response payload, update a log entry's metadata, and delete log entries that match given criteria.
ai-search-core: Cloudflare AI Search instances: create, list, inspect, update, move between namespaces, and delete them. Run semantic search or chat completions grounded in indexed content, on one instance or several at once with merged results. Also purge cached search results and view usage and indexing stats.
ai-search-items: Cloudflare AI Search items, the files and documents indexed in an AI Search instance. Upload files, create or update items, and sync an item to the index. List and inspect items, view their text chunks and processing logs, download the original file, and delete an item with its indexed data.
ai-search-jobs: Cloudflare AI Search indexing jobs: start a new indexing job for an AI Search instance, list past and current jobs, check the details and status of one job, view its log entries, and cancel a job that is still running.
ai-search-namespace: Cloudflare AI Search namespaces, which group AI Search instances: create, list, view, and delete namespaces, and change a namespace's description or public endpoint settings. A namespace must be empty before deletion, and the default namespace cannot be deleted.
ai-search-tokens: AI Search service tokens: stored Cloudflare credentials that let an AI Search instance access its data source. Create, list, inspect (secret not shown), replace, and delete them. Replacing a token invalidates cached credentials for instances using it, and tokens in use by an instance cannot be deleted.
ai-security-api: Cloudflare AI Security for Apps, which scans prompts sent to LLM endpoints labeled cf-llm for personal data, unsafe topics, and prompt injection. Check or turn detection on or off for a zone, and view or replace the custom topic categories used to score prompts. Results feed custom and rate limiting rules.
alerting-api: Cloudflare Notifications (alerting): create, update, test and delete notification policies, see which alert types and delivery methods an account can use, set up PagerDuty and webhook destinations, mute alerts with silences, unsubscribe an email address from a policy, and view the history of sent notifications.
analytics-api: Cloudflare analytics: query dataset stats as summaries with period-over-period comparison, time series, or top N rankings. Run SQL queries against account analytics datasets and list available datasets and columns. Also covers Argo Smart Routing latency and bandwidth analytics per zone and per location, and CASB data security findings (summary, time series, top integrations).
analytics-engine-api: Workers Analytics Engine: run SQL queries against the event data your Workers have written to Analytics Engine datasets. Send the query as plain text in the request body, suited to longer queries. Results return as newline-delimited JSON, or as one JSON object with a FORMAT JSON clause.
api-security-schema-validation: Cloudflare API Shield schema validation: upload, list, inspect, delete, and enable or disable OpenAPI schemas, and list the hosts and operations they cover. Also manage zone-wide validation settings and per-operation settings (get, update, bulk edit, reset to zone defaults).
api-security-token-validation: Cloudflare API Shield JWT token validation for a zone: create, view, update and delete JWT validation configurations, replace or edit their signing keys (credentials), and manage token validation rules singly or in bulk, including reordering and filtering by configuration, action, state, or host.
api-security-vulnerability-scanner: Cloudflare API Security vulnerability scanner: start, list, inspect and delete vulnerability scans of your APIs; manage target environments to scan; keep credential sets and the credentials inside them for authenticated scans; and view or replace the zone's session identifiers (header, cookie or JWT claim) that distinguish API sessions.
argo-api: Cloudflare Argo: turn Argo Smart Routing on or off for a zone and check its current setting, count how many zones have it enabled for an account or user, and view or change the Tiered Cache setting, which routes cache misses through upper-tier data centers to reduce load on the origin.
artifacts-api: Cloudflare Artifacts, Git-compatible repository hosting: create, list, fork, import (from an HTTPS Git URL) and delete repositories, and manage namespaces. Browse contents by ref: file bytes, raw files, commit history, commits, trees and blobs. Create, list and revoke scoped Git access tokens.
audit-logs-api: Cloudflare audit logs: list the record of changes made in an account, filtered by who made the change, which zone it affected, and the time range. Use it to find who changed a setting and when. Read-only.
basin-catalog-api: Basin Catalog (R2 Data Catalog), which turns R2 buckets into Apache Iceberg catalogs: enable, disable, list, inspect and delete catalogs, store and check catalog credentials, browse namespaces and tables with full Iceberg metadata, and view or change maintenance settings for catalogs and tables, including queuing maintenance and listing recent runs.
billing-api: Cloudflare billing: create, view, update and delete the account billing profile, billing email and locale, payment method setup, and billing address validation. Also look up rate plan details, manage spend policies (usage-block or notification limits, with change history and evaluation audit), and query billable usage, cost and metrics.
bot-management-api: Cloudflare Bot Management for a zone: view and update the bot detection configuration, and submit feedback reports on misclassified traffic (false positives where legitimate traffic is flagged as a bot, false negatives where bots are missed), optionally scoped to a traffic sample by filter expression. Also lists past feedback reports.
botnet-feed-api: Cloudflare DDoS Botnet Threat Feed for ASNs registered to your account: list the registered ASNs, remove an ASN from the feed, and get botnet tracking data for an ASN, either a full report or a single day's report (defaults to the previous day).
brand-protection-api: Cloudflare Brand Protection: manage saved brand and logo queries, list domain matches and logo matches for lookalike or phishing domains, dismiss or restore matches singly or in bulk, upload an image to find the closest visually similar scanned images, run an AI scan of domains for brand impersonation, and count saved queries.
browser-run-core: Cloudflare Browser Run (browser rendering): start a crawl of a URL and its linked pages with page-load and wait controls, check a crawl's results, and cancel a running crawl. Also retrieves session recordings as events per target, and network activity for a target, optionally as a HAR file.
browser-run-devtools: Cloudflare Browser Run DevTools: start and close remote browser sessions (with optional traffic guardrails), list and inspect active sessions, and get browser version info. Manage tabs and other debuggable targets (open, list, inspect, bring to front, close), create live view links (view-only optional), and fetch the Chrome DevTools Protocol schema.
browser-run-quick-action: Cloudflare Browser Run quick actions: one-call operations on a web page from a URL or raw HTML. Get rendered HTML, markdown, or a PDF, take a screenshot, or get HTML plus screenshot together. Also extract links, the accessibility tree, element text and dimensions by CSS selector, or structured JSON using a prompt or schema.
builds-core: Cloudflare Workers Builds (CI for Workers): start a build for a branch or commit, cancel one, check its status and logs, list builds for a Worker, and find builds by Worker version. Also covers repository connections, auto-detecting repo build configuration, build tokens, and build-minute limits.
builds-deploy-hooks: Workers Builds deploy hooks: create HTTP hooks that start a build for a chosen Worker branch, list and inspect a Worker's hooks, rename a hook or change its target branch, delete a hook, and trigger a build by calling a hook's secret UUID, which needs no authentication.
builds-triggers: Workers Builds triggers, which control how a Worker is built automatically from a connected repository: create, list, update and delete triggers (build and deploy commands, branch and path filters, cache setting, build token), manage build-time environment variables and secrets, and purge the build cache.
builds-workers: Workers Builds, Cloudflare's git-based CI for Workers: connect a Worker to a repository with its production build settings, view the current repository and build configuration, update git, production, or preview build settings, and remove a Worker's build settings and triggers (cancels unfinished builds, keeps the Worker).
cache-api: Cloudflare cache for a zone: purge or mark cached content stale (zone-wide or per environment), Tiered Cache settings (Smart and Regional), Cache Reserve (enable, check status, clear), image variants caching, and mappings of origin IPs to cloud vendor regions for tiered cache routing.
client-side-security-api: Cloudflare Client-Side Security (Page Shield) for a zone: view scripts, outbound webpage connections, and cookies detected on pages, manage content security rules (create, view, update, delete) that apply an action when a filter expression matches, and turn the product on or off and set its reporting behavior.
cloud-connector-api: Cloudflare Cloud Connector rules for a zone: list the current rules that route traffic to a cloud service, and replace the zone's whole rule set with an updated configuration.
cloudforce-one-credential-monitor: Cloudflare Cloudforce One credential monitoring: register domains to watch for leaked or compromised credentials, list the registered domains, remove a domain from monitoring, and list credential matches found for the account's monitored domains.
cloudforce-one-priority-intelligence: Cloudflare Cloudforce One Priority Intelligence: create, update, list and delete Priority Intelligence Requirements (PIRs) and check quota; turn plain-language requirements into Threat Events filters; review matched events, counts, daily trends and triage; manage the organization profile; and run structured interests with evaluations and backtests.
cloudforce-one-requests: Cloudforce One requests for information (RFIs): create, list, view and update requests, and read or send messages on them (including publishing drafts). Upload, list and download request file assets. Look up request types, priorities, statuses, TLP levels and custom metadata fields, check token quota, legal-response access, and your project profile.
cloudforce-one-rules: Cloudflare Cloudforce One detection rules: create, validate, update, search, list and delete rules, plus a dashboard stats view and a folder tree. Also structured email rules (field catalog, test against sample email, validate), the approval workflow (list, cancel, resubmit, edit pending), per-account exemption patterns, and managed rule metadata.
cloudforce-one-scans: Cloudforce One network scanning: create, list, edit and delete scan configurations, and retrieve the latest results for a configuration, including discovered open ports and the service banners grabbed from those ports.
cloudforce-one-threat-intel: Cloudflare Cloudforce One threat intelligence: datasets with account groups and read/write access grants; threat events (create, bulk edit, copy, move, search, aggregate, GraphQL, saved queries, relationships, raw data); indicators and indicator types; tags, tag categories and threat actors; event categories, attackers, countries and target industries; cross-entity search; malware binary upload and retrieval.
cloudforce-one-threat-signals: Cloudforce One Threat Signals: subscribe to and manage threat intelligence feeds (poll, view raw), browse, search and read articles, see summaries, relevance to Priority Intelligence Requirements and severity counts, mark read, reprocess, tag, list extracted indicators (IOCs), and create and run custom AI skills.
connector-interrupts-api: Cloudflare Magic WAN Connector interrupts: create an interrupt for a Magic WAN Connector device and list the interrupts that exist for a connector.
connector-telemetry-events-api: Magic WAN Connector telemetry events: list the events a connector has reported, and fetch the details of a single event. Use these to check what happened on a Magic WAN Connector device, such as its status changes and activity history.
connector-telemetry-snapshots-api: Cloudflare Magic WAN Connector telemetry snapshots: list the snapshots a connector device has reported and fetch a single snapshot, for checking the device's recent state and health.
connectors-api: Cloudflare Magic WAN Connectors, the on-premises devices that link a site to Magic WAN. Create, list, inspect, update, edit and delete connectors, and re-provision a connector's license key.
content-scan-api: Cloudflare Content Scanning, which scans uploaded content in requests for a zone: check whether scanning is on and when it last changed, turn it on or off, and manage custom expressions (list, add, edit, delete) that tell the scanner where to find content it can't detect on its own, such as files inside JSON bodies.
cps-api: Cloudflare communication preferences for the authenticated user: view email verification status, marketing email opt-in or opt-out state, and language locale, and update subscription choices and locale. Email verification settings cannot be changed here.
csam-scanner-api: Cloudflare CSAM Scanner, which detects known child sexual abuse material in cached content: view a zone's current scanner configuration, and update it to turn scanning on or off and change its settings.
custom-csrs-api: Cloudflare custom Certificate Signing Requests (CSRs): generate a CSR for an account or zone, with Cloudflare creating and securely storing the private key, then list CSRs, view details of one, or delete a CSR together with its private key. Use this to get a certificate issued by a certificate authority.
custom-hostnames-api: Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostnames: create, list, search, inspect, edit and delete customer hostnames with SSL certificate issuance and domain validation (http, txt, email), bundled RSA/ECDSA certificates and replacing or removing a certificate in a pack, the zone's fallback origin, and custom hostname quota usage.
custom-nameservers-api: Cloudflare custom nameservers (vanity nameservers): add a custom nameserver to an account or zone so zones can use your own domain's nameserver names instead of Cloudflare's defaults, list the custom nameservers already configured, and remove one from the account.
custom-pages-api: Cloudflare Custom Pages: view and update which custom page is shown for each error or challenge type (such as block or rate-limit pages) at the account or zone level, manage the custom assets (uploaded page content) behind them, and generate signed preview tokens to check a page before publishing.
diagnostics-api: Cloudflare diagnostics: create, list, view, update and delete endpoint health checks that monitor whether an endpoint is reachable and responding, and run traceroutes from Cloudflare data centers (colos) to a target to see the network path and troubleshoot connectivity.
dls-api: Cloudflare Data Localization Suite (DLS) regional services: list and inspect the available regions (managed and custom), and bind CIDRs from a BYOIP prefix to a region so traffic is handled there. Create, view, change the region of, and delete these prefix bindings.
dns-dnssec: Cloudflare DNSSEC for a zone: check whether DNSSEC is enabled and view its configuration, turn it on or off, delete the DNSSEC configuration, and list the Zone Signing Keys (ZSKs) used to sign the zone's DNS records.
dns-domainconnect: Cloudflare DNS Domain Connect, the protocol that lets external service providers set up DNS records for a domain: check a domain's Domain Connect settings, get provider configuration and provider templates, verify signed requests against DNS TXT public keys, and a service health heartbeat check.
dns-firewall-api: Cloudflare DNS Firewall clusters: create, list, view, modify and delete the clusters for an account, and view or update each cluster's reverse DNS (PTR record) configuration.
dns-records: Cloudflare DNS records for a zone: create, get, list/search/filter, edit, overwrite and delete records, run several changes together as a batch, import or export a BIND zone file, and scan the domain for existing records, then review and accept or reject the findings.
dns-settings: Cloudflare DNS settings: view and update account-level or zone-level DNS defaults, manage Custom Nameserver Sets (create, list, get, rename, delete unassigned sets), and manage Internal DNS Views for an account (create, list, get, update, delete).
dns-zone-transfers: Cloudflare DNS zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR): set up secondary zones that pull from external primaries and primary zones that send to secondaries. Manage peers, ACLs and TSIG keys, enable or disable outgoing transfers, force an AXFR or notify secondaries, check transfer status, and view DNS record usage and quota.
email-auth-api: Cloudflare email authentication for a zone: view and change the DMARC report configuration and its status, and inspect an SPF TXT record to get a parsed breakdown of its structure.
email-domains-api: Cloudflare email sending domains (pilot-account only, behind a default-off gate): enroll a domain and get its four DNS records, list and inspect domains and their status, trigger a re-check of customer DNS, delete a domain, and read the change feed (with removal tombstones) for syncing state.
email-security-allow-policies: Cloudflare Email Security allow policies, which exempt emails matching a sender pattern from security detections: create, list (with filters), inspect, partially edit, fully replace, and delete policies, or run several create, update and delete changes together in one atomic batch. Creating a policy bypasses scanning.
email-security-block-senders: Cloudflare Email Security blocked sender patterns: block mail from email addresses, domains, or IP addresses (regular expressions supported). List and search patterns, filtering by type, view one, create, partially edit, fully replace, or delete them, and run several changes together in one atomic batch.
email-security-bulk-actions: Cloudflare Email Security bulk action jobs: create a job to move or release many messages matching a search, list jobs and check a job's status, see the individual messages in a job with their processing status, cancel a running job, and delete finished jobs.
email-security-content-policies: Cloudflare Email Security content policies, which apply an action to emails whose subject or body matches a pattern: create, list (filter by name or enabled status, or search names and patterns), view, edit, and delete policies, plus run several delete, update, or create operations together in one atomic batch.
email-security-core: Cloudflare Email Security core: view the trailing 12-month aggregated report of detections, dispositions, and policy activity, and list PhishGuard threat alert reports for a date range. Submit messages for reclassification or to report missed detections (false negatives and false positives), and track submission status and outcomes.
email-security-domains: Cloudflare Email Security protected domains: add a domain for protection, list and inspect domains (delivery mode, SPF/DMARC status, authorization state), edit some settings or replace the full configuration, remove a domain, run several domain changes in one batch request, and get the DNS TXT record for verifying ownership.
email-security-impersonation-registry: Cloudflare Email Security impersonation registry: the list of people and email addresses to protect from impersonation. Add entries (regex patterns supported), list and inspect them, edit or remove them. Shows whether an entry was added manually or synced from a directory; synced entries can't be edited.
email-security-investigate: Cloudflare Email Security message investigation: search emails and open one message for headers, recipients, sender and quarantine status. View detection details, raw EML, body previews (detection or non-detection), delivery trace, and post-delivery action log. Move messages between mailbox folders or release quarantined ones.
email-security-sending-domain-restrictio: Cloudflare Email Security sending domain restrictions: require TLS for inbound mail from a given sender domain, so mail without TLS is dropped. Create, list (with search and sorting), view, edit and delete restrictions, and exempt specific subdomains from the TLS requirement.
email-security-trusted-domains: Cloudflare Email Security trusted domains: list, view, create, edit, replace and delete trusted domain patterns (exact or regex) for partner domains and approved senders, so they skip recent-domain-registration and lookalike/spoof checks. Also run several changes together in one atomic batch.
email-security-url-ignore-patterns: Cloudflare Email Security URL rewrite ignore patterns: list, view, create, edit and delete patterns for URLs that should not be rewritten in email links, or apply several changes at once in a single atomic batch. Deleting a pattern makes matching URLs get rewritten again.
field-extractors-api: Cloudflare field extractors: view the custom extraction rules set for an extractor type, replace the full rule set (any rules left out are deleted), or delete all custom rules for that type.
firewall-api: Cloudflare firewall rules: IP Access rules to allow, block or challenge traffic by IP, IP range, country or ASN for an account or zone; Zone Lockdown rules that restrict URLs to approved IPs; User Agent Blocking rules for a zone; and the payload logging public key (Enterprise) used to encrypt matched payloads.
flagship-api: Cloudflare Flagship feature flags: create, list, rename and delete apps; create, read, update, patch (enable/disable, default variation) and delete flags; view a flag's change history; evaluate flags against a user context; fetch flag definitions for local evaluation in SDKs.
fraud-api: Cloudflare Fraud Detection settings for a zone: read the current configuration and update it. Applies per zone, so use it to check or change how fraud detection is set up for a given domain.
google-tag-gateway-api: Cloudflare Google Tag Gateway, which serves Google tag (gtag, Tag Manager) scripts and measurement traffic through your own zone's domain: read the current Google Tag Gateway settings for a zone and update them.
healthchecks-api: Cloudflare Health Checks, which monitor whether an origin server is up: create, list, view, update (full or partial edit) and delete health checks. Also create, view and delete preview health checks, which let you test a configuration before saving it as a real check.
hyperdrive-api: Cloudflare Hyperdrive configurations for connecting Workers to external databases: create, list, inspect, partially update, fully replace and delete configurations (origin connection, caching, mTLS, connection limits), restart the connection pool, and get a signed authorization for creating a Cloudflare-billed PlanetScale database.
iam-oauth-clients: Cloudflare IAM OAuth clients for an account: create, list, inspect, update and delete OAuth clients, and rotate a client secret without downtime by issuing a second secret, then deleting the old rotated secret once your configuration uses the new one.
iam-resource-groups: Cloudflare IAM resource groups: create, list, view, update and delete resource groups on an account. Resource groups bundle account resources so access can be scoped to them, for example when assigning permissions to members or API tokens.
iam-sso: Cloudflare account SSO connectors for logging into Cloudflare through an identity provider: create, list, inspect, update (state or configuration) and delete connectors, and start domain ownership verification once the DNS TXT record has been added.
iam-user-groups: Cloudflare IAM user groups: create, list, inspect, update and delete user groups on an account, add, list, inspect, replace and remove group members, and look up the account's permission groups and the available OAuth scopes.
images-core: Cloudflare Images: upload images (directly or via one-time upload URLs for browser and mobile clients), list, inspect, edit metadata or access control, download, and delete them. Also covers storage usage and image count stats, signing keys for signed URLs, and zone transformation flows configuration.
images-import: Cloudflare Images bulk import from Amazon S3: configure, list, rename, delete and verify S3 sources (including testing credentials before saving), then create, start, abort and delete imports from a source, and check import status, progress and object counts, and logs.
images-variants: Cloudflare Images variants: named presets that resize and transform stored images for different uses, such as thumbnails or banners. Create, list, inspect, update and delete variants. Editing or deleting a variant purges the cache for all images served with it.
intel-core: Cloudflare threat intelligence lookups: ASN overview and subnets, IP geolocation, ASN and threat categories, available IP list categories, domains that resolved to an IP, domain and URL security details and categories (single or bulk), domain category history, WHOIS records, Security Center issue types, and domain recategorization requests.
intel-indicator-feeds: Cloudflare Intel custom threat indicator feeds for sharing threat intelligence: create, list, inspect and update feeds, read or download their raw entries, replace feed data with a new snapshot, check the status of asynchronous uploads, grant or revoke other accounts' access, and create feed providers (Intel accounts only).
intel-sinkholes: Cloudflare sinkholes for redirecting malicious traffic: create, list, inspect, rename, reconfigure and delete sinkholes, including optional R2 storage of full request bodies. Also manage each sinkhole's ingress rules, which tie a BYOIP CIDR block and a Spectrum-enabled zone to it: create, list, get, replace and delete.
internal-api: Cloudflare internal route for testing URL submissions. It has a single tool that creates a test URL submission. It is not meant for general use and covers no other tasks.
ips-api: Cloudflare IP ranges: list the IP addresses used by the Cloudflare network and by the JD Cloud network (Cloudflare's China network partner), for building firewall allowlists or checking that traffic comes from Cloudflare.
k2-api: K2 streams: create, list or filter, inspect, update and delete streams in an account. Configure inputs, including HTTP ingestion with authentication and CORS origins. Also list the subscriptions on a stream, with lag per subscription.
leaked-credential-checks-api: Cloudflare Leaked Credential Checks, which flags requests carrying usernames and passwords exposed in known data breaches: turn detection on or off for a zone and see its status, and create, list, inspect, update and delete custom detection locations (username and password expressions) for where credentials appear in requests.
live-api: Cloudflare liveness check. Runs a single health probe and returns a success message to confirm the service is up and responding. It has no other functions and does not manage or change any resources.
load-balancers-account: Cloudflare Load Balancers managed at the account level (these can also be scoped to a zone): create, list, inspect, update, edit and delete load balancers, and check the account's current load balancer resource usage counts.
load-balancers-core: Cloudflare Load Balancing, read-only lookups: list region mappings or fetch a single one, search across load balancing resources (load balancers, pools, monitors), and retrieve the result of an earlier load balancer preview by its preview ID.
load-balancers-monitor-groups: Cloudflare Load Balancing monitor groups: create, list, fetch, update, edit (partial changes) and delete groups of health monitors, and see which resources, such as load balancer pools, reference a given monitor group before changing or removing it.
load-balancers-monitors: Cloudflare Load Balancing health monitors: create, list, fetch, update, edit and delete the health checks that probe origin servers in load balancer pools, preview a monitor's results against pools before saving it, and see which pools or other resources reference a monitor.
load-balancers-pools: Cloudflare Load Balancing pools (groups of origin servers): create, list, get, update, edit and delete pools, bulk edit many pools at once, check a pool's current health, preview health using monitor settings, and see which load balancers or other resources reference a pool.
logpush-api: Cloudflare Logpush for sending logs to external destinations: create, list, inspect, update and delete push jobs, see available dataset fields, validate destinations and ownership challenges, check logpull origin options, start Instant Logs for a zone, and manage custom SQL log transformers with preview and version history.
logs-api: Cloudflare Logs: pull edge HTTP request logs by time range or by Ray ID, list available log fields, and fetch logs stored in R2. Manage Log Explorer datasets (list, create, update, delete) and run SQL queries on them. Also covers the Logpull retention flag and CMB (Customer Metadata Boundary) config.
magic-network-monitoring-api: Cloudflare Magic Network Monitoring: create, view, update and delete the account's monitoring configuration (default sampling rate, router IPs, WARP devices), manage alert rules singly or in bulk of up to 100, change a rule's advertisement setting, and generate a token for exporting VPC flow logs.
magic-transit-advanced-dns-protection: Cloudflare Magic Transit Advanced DNS Protection: manage an account's DNS Protection rules. Create rules, list them, get one by its ID, update or delete a single rule, or delete all of the account's rules at once.
magic-transit-advanced-tcp-protection: Magic Transit Advanced TCP Protection against TCP-based DDoS attacks: manage protected prefixes (singly or in bulk) and allowlisted prefixes, SYN Protection rules and filters, TCP Flow Protection rules and filters, and turn account-level TCP protection on or off. Also reads and updates account BGP settings (default ASN, route redistribution).
magic-transit-apps: Cloudflare Magic Transit apps: create, list, update and delete the apps defined on an account. Use these to manage the account's custom app definitions for Magic Transit and Magic WAN.
magic-transit-bgp-filter-profiles: Cloudflare Magic Transit BGP filter profiles: create, list, view, update, and delete the profiles that hold BGP filtering settings for an account. Updates change only the properties you send, and the description can be cleared.
magic-transit-cf-interconnects: Cloudflare Magic Transit CF Interconnects: list the interconnects on an account, view details of one, and update a single interconnect or many at once. Updates can run in validate-only mode to check changes without saving them.
magic-transit-cf1-sites: Cloudflare Magic Transit CF1 Sites: create, list, view, update and delete sites, which are physical customer network locations with optional geographic coordinates. Also manage each site's ramps (network connections such as GRE tunnels, IPsec tunnels, interconnects, and MCONN links): add, list, inspect and remove them.
magic-transit-gre-tunnels: Cloudflare Magic Transit GRE tunnels: list GRE tunnels on an account, view one tunnel's details, create tunnels, update one or many tunnels in bulk, and disable and delete a tunnel. Create, update and delete support a validate-only dry run that checks changes without saving them.
magic-transit-ipsec-tunnels: Magic Transit IPsec tunnels: create, list, inspect, update (singly or in bulk) and delete IPsec tunnels on an account, generate a pre-shared key for a tunnel's IKE session, or set pre-shared keys for several tunnels at once. Changes can be validated without being saved. Keys cannot be retrieved later.
magic-transit-pcaps: Magic Transit packet captures (PCAPs): start sample or full packet capture requests, list them, check one by id, stop a full capture, and download the resulting PCAP file. Also register, list, validate and delete the AWS or GCP storage buckets used for full captures.
magic-transit-redundancy-groups: Cloudflare Magic Transit redundancy groups: create, list, inspect, update and delete groups of tunnels that act together for failover. View each group's member tunnels, and rename a group or replace its members. Deleting a group keeps its tunnels and clears their group assignment.
magic-transit-routes: Cloudflare Magic Transit static routes: list and inspect routes, create a route, update one route or many at once, and delete one route or several in bulk. Create and update calls can run in validate-only mode to check changes without saving them.
magic-transit-sites: Cloudflare Magic Transit sites (branch/office locations): create, list, view, update and delete sites, including lookup by connector. Also manage each site's LANs (with high availability addressing), WANs, ACLs, app configurations, and NetFlow export settings.
managed-defense-api: Cloudflare Managed Defense vulnerability discovery: create upload repositories or import deployed Workers by name, get one-hour upload tokens, and check repository source readiness and scan history. Submit scan requests for operator review, list scans and track their status, and retrieve the reviewed scan reports.
managed-transforms-api: Cloudflare Managed Transforms: list the available managed HTTP request and response header transforms and whether each is enabled, turn one or more on or off, or disable all of them at once.
mcp-api: Cloudflare MCP portals and servers for governing AI tool access through Cloudflare Access: create, list, inspect, update and delete portals; register upstream MCP servers, update their configuration and credentials, and sync their capabilities to check connection errors; and view daily or monthly tool-call counts per portal, server, or account.
media-api: Cloudflare Media usage analytics. Retrieve usage for an account or zone, returning the same Stream metrics as the Stream usage endpoint, such as minutes of video viewed (streamMinutesViewed). Read-only reporting; it has no tools for uploading or managing media.
mesh-api: Cloudflare Mesh nodes: create, list, filter, inspect, edit and delete nodes in an account. Also covers connector and connection details, the token that links a WARP device to a node, high-availability configuration, and manual failover to make a chosen client the active connector.
monetization-api: Cloudflare Monetization Gateway: check whether an account or zone is eligible and view the latest eligibility decision, and manage a zone's Payment Required (HTTP 402) rules by listing, getting, replacing the whole ruleset, editing one rule, deleting one rule, or deleting all rules.
network-api: Cloudflare private networking for Tunnel and WARP: create, edit, list and delete private network (CIDR) routes and hostname routes through a Tunnel, and look up which routes match an IP address. Also manages WARP IP assignment subnets, Cloudflare Source and Initial Resolved IP default subnets, and virtual networks.
network-interconnects-api: Cloudflare Network Interconnect: create, view, update and delete physical and virtual interconnects between Cloudflare and external networks, and Cloud Network Interconnects (CNIs) for private cloud connectivity. Check link status, download the Letter of Authorization (LOA) and its default customer name, list available slots, and read or change settings.
o11y-core: Cloudflare Workers Observability: view event counts and sizes by dataset and service per day (up to 90 days), list AI agent conversation sessions and the traces within each session, list and set up metrics export, and create or fetch shared queries that save query results to share with others.
o11y-destinations: Workers Observability telemetry destinations, the external endpoints that receive telemetry (such as logs and traces) from Workers. List your destinations, create new ones, update the configuration of an existing destination, and delete destinations you no longer need.
o11y-issues: Cloudflare observability issues: list and inspect detected issues and their error occurrences, get account issue counts, change issue status or group title, group, add to, remove from or ungroup issues, send an issue to notification policies, and create, edit, list or delete issue automations.
o11y-queries: Cloudflare Workers Observability saved queries: save a query for reuse, list all saved queries, retrieve one, update it, and delete it. Use this group to manage the stored query definitions, not to run queries or read telemetry.
o11y-telemetry: Cloudflare Workers Observability telemetry: run temporary or saved queries over your telemetry events, list the keys present in events, list the unique values for a key, and set up live tail (websocket) to stream events in real time, with a heartbeat to keep the session active.
o11y-tracing: Cloudflare Traces (distributed tracing) configuration for a zone: view, update, or reset zone-level tracing settings to defaults (sampling rules are kept), and get, replace, or delete the ordered sampling override rules that control which requests are traced.
observability-api: Workers Observability usage limits: check whether the account is currently keeping fewer of its events (usually because it passed its daily limit), and see what that limit is. Limits reset at 00:00 UTC, and paid accounts are restored in stages over the following hours.
organization-api: Cloudflare organizations: create, view, rename and delete organizations (including sub-organizations), list the accounts attached to one, manage members (add singly or in batch, view, remove), accept or reject invitations, view and edit the business profile (name, email, phone, address), and list organization shares.
organizations-api: Cloudflare Organizations: view cost and usage data (billing) across all accounts in an organization, list the organization's audit logs of who changed what, and see the chronological change history of a resource from a given audit log entry.
page-rules-core: Cloudflare Page Rules for a zone: create, list, and inspect URL-pattern rules that apply settings or actions to matching requests, such as redirects or cache behavior. Edit individual fields of a rule, replace its whole configuration, or delete it.
pages-api: Cloudflare Pages sites: create, list, edit and delete projects (build, deployment and environment variable settings), connect or disconnect a GitHub/GitLab repo, create, list, retry, roll back and delete deployments, view build logs, purge the build cache, and attach, validate and remove custom domains.
pay-per-crawl-api: Cloudflare Pay Per Crawl, which lets sites charge AI crawlers for access: create, view and change a zone's pay-per-crawl config, link Stripe accounts for publishers and crawlers, list known crawlers, read and sign the terms and conditions, and check or set which zones are eligible to enable it.
pay-per-use-api: Cloudflare Pay Per Use, where publishers charge operators (crawlers/AI buyers) for content access: configure operator accounts, enable zones and check eligibility, list operators and set, propose, accept, reject, opt out of or resume prices, review price proposals, list licensed domains, submit usage reports, and view usage and earnings stats.
pipelines-api: Cloudflare Pipelines for streaming data ingestion: create, list, inspect and delete streams (data entry points, which can be updated), sinks (destinations where data is written), and pipelines that connect a stream to a sink using SQL transformations. Also checks that pipeline SQL is valid before use.
precursor-api: Cloudflare Precursor settings for a zone. Read a zone's current Precursor configuration, including its detection mode, and update that configuration. The group only covers reading and changing the zone-level settings.
previews-api: Cloudflare previews: delete a Preview by ID, removing a preview deployment that is no longer needed. This group only supports deletion; it cannot create, list, or inspect previews.
radar-ai: Cloudflare Radar AI traffic and usage data: AI bot HTTP request volume over time, summaries and breakdowns by dimension, Workers AI inference counts (summary and grouped over time), and the median HTML-to-markdown size reduction for AI agent requests, as a total or a time series.
radar-annotations: Cloudflare Radar annotations: look up the latest Internet outages and anomalies, see outage counts by location, list recent annotations (events that explain changes in traffic data), and fetch a single annotation by ID.
radar-as112: Cloudflare Radar data on AS112, the public sink for reverse-DNS and private-address lookups: query volume over time, the share of queries split by dimension (as a summary or over time), and the top locations by query count, including those using DNSSEC, EDNS, or a given IP version.
radar-attacks: Cloudflare Radar DDoS attack statistics for layer 3 (network) and layer 7 (application) attacks: trends over time, breakdowns by dimension (such as attack type), top origin and target locations, top attacking autonomous systems (layer 7), and the top origin-to-target attack routes.
radar-bgp: Cloudflare Radar BGP routing data: hijack and route leak events, real-time routes for a prefix, AS paths to tier-1 networks, upstream share over time, MOAS prefixes, prefix-to-ASN mapping, routing table stats, announced IP space by AS, BGP update volumes and top ASes or prefixes, and RPKI ROA validation and ASPA objects, changes and counts.
radar-bots: Cloudflare Radar bot traffic data: look up a specific bot or list known bots, see HTTP request volume from bots over time, and get summaries or over-time distributions of bot requests broken down by a chosen dimension. Also covers web crawler traffic with the same summary and breakdown views.
radar-core: Cloudflare Radar core data: AI agent readiness scores across scanned domains, downloadable datasets, geolocation lookup, leaked credential trends in login requests, post-quantum encryption (origin stats, and a hostname or IP TLS test), robots.txt top user agents and domain categories, TCP resets and timeouts, traffic anomalies and outages, and global search.
radar-ct: Cloudflare Radar Certificate Transparency data: list and look up certificate authorities and CT logs, get certificate issuance volume over time, and see summaries or time-based breakdowns of certificates grouped by a dimension such as authority or log.
radar-dns: Cloudflare Radar DNS statistics from the 1.1.1.1 resolver: query volume over time, the breakdown of queries by a chosen dimension (as a summary or as a time series), and the top autonomous systems (networks) and top locations by DNS query volume.
radar-email: Cloudflare Radar email traffic data: breakdowns of email routing and email security metrics by dimension, as a snapshot or over time, plus top TLDs by email volume and by share classified as malicious, spam, or spoofed.
radar-entities: Cloudflare Radar entity lookups: find autonomous systems (ASNs) by number or IP address, list them, see their AS-SET memberships and AS-level relationships with other networks, and rank ASes by presence in the botnet threat feed. Also look up countries/locations and get information about an IP address.
radar-http: Cloudflare Radar HTTP traffic statistics: rank the top autonomous systems (networks) or countries/locations by HTTP requests, overall or filtered by bot class, browser family, device type, HTTP method, HTTP protocol version, IP version, operating system, or TLS version. Also HTTP request volume over time and its distribution by dimension.
radar-netflows: Cloudflare Radar NetFlows: view network traffic volume over time, see how traffic is distributed by a chosen dimension (as a summary or as a time series by group), and rank the top autonomous systems (ASes) and top locations by traffic.
radar-origins: Cloudflare Radar origins: list cloud provider origins (such as hyperscaler regions) and look up one with its regions, get aggregated summaries of origin metrics broken down by a chosen dimension, and view an origin's metrics over time, either as a time series or as a distribution by dimension.
radar-quality: Cloudflare Radar internet quality: Internet Quality Index (IQI) summaries and time series of bandwidth, latency, and DNS response time percentiles, plus Cloudflare Speed Test results from the last 90 days. Speed Test tools give bandwidth, latency, jitter, and packet loss summaries, histograms, and rankings of top networks (ASes) and locations.
radar-ranking: Cloudflare Radar rankings: look up the rank of a domain, list top or trending domains, and see how domain ranks change over time. Also covers top Internet services (apps and platforms), their categories, and rank changes over time. Exact ranks are given for the top 100 domains, with buckets beyond that.
radar-tlds: Cloudflare Radar top-level domain (TLD) data: list TLDs and look up details for a specific one, plus authoritative nameserver performance for TLDs, as a summary or a timeseries over time, grouped by a chosen dimension.
ready-api: Cloudflare readiness check. A single tool that runs the service's readiness checks and returns a success message if they pass, for confirming the API is up and responding.
realtime-kit: Cloudflare RealtimeKit for video/audio meetings: manage apps, meetings, participants and their auth tokens, and presets. Control live sessions (polls, mute, kick), start and stop livestreams and recordings (including audio tracks), export chat, transcripts and summaries, view session and peer stats, usage and livestream analytics, and configure webhooks.
realtime-moq: Cloudflare Realtime MoQ (Media over QUIC) relays: create, list, inspect, rename or reconfigure, and delete relays, plus manage each relay's access tokens by minting new relay-scoped tokens, listing the ones it accepts (without secrets), and revoking them.
realtime-sfu: Cloudflare Realtime SFU apps, the isolated namespaces in which WebRTC sessions access tracks: create new apps, list all apps in the account, view the details of one app, update an app, and delete an app.
realtime-turn: Cloudflare Realtime TURN keys, used for relaying WebRTC traffic: create new TURN keys, list all keys in the account, view a single key's details, update a key, and delete a key.
registrar-api: Cloudflare Registrar for domain names: search for name suggestions, check availability, register a domain (billable), check eligibility and start transfers in from another registrar, update an existing registration, list and view domains on the account, track registration, transfer and update workflow status, and look up supported TLD extensions.
registrar-sandbox-api: Cloudflare Registrar sandbox for testing domain registration: search for domain name suggestions from a keyword, check real-time availability, start a registration, update an existing registration, list and inspect registrations on the account, track registration and update workflow status, and look up supported extensions (TLDs) with their input schemas.
reporting-api: Cloudflare reporting: view and change an account's industry classification, list reporting policies or fetch one by ID, and list generated reports or fetch a single report by ID. Policies and reports are read-only here; only the industry setting can be edited.
request-tracers-api: Cloudflare Request Tracer: run a simulated HTTP request through Cloudflare's edge to see how rules and settings would handle it, without sending real traffic. Useful for debugging firewall rules, page rules, and request transformations. Supports custom headers, cookies, body, and geolocation context.
resource-sharing-api: Cloudflare Resource Sharing: create, list, rename and delete shares that give other accounts or whole organizations access to your Cloudflare resources. Add, update and remove the shared resources, manage recipient accounts on account-targeted shares, and exclude specific accounts from organization-wide shares.
rules-api: Cloudflare account-level lists, reusable sets of items such as IPs that rules can reference. Create, view, rename the description of, and delete lists. Add, read, remove, or replace all items in a list, and check the status of asynchronous bulk operations.
rulesets-core: Cloudflare Rulesets engine, core operations at account or zone level: create, list, fetch, update and delete rulesets, get or replace the entry point ruleset for a phase, and add, edit or remove individual rules in a ruleset. Updates create a new ruleset version.
rum-api: Cloudflare Web Analytics (RUM): create, view, update and delete Web Analytics sites for an account, list site tags and zone tags, validate a hostname, and manage the rules in a site's ruleset (list, create, update, delete, or change several rules in one request).
scim-api: Cloudflare SCIM 2.0 provisioning for identity providers: create, list, get, update, patch and delete account members (users) and user groups, including group membership and deprovisioning users. Also discovery of the service provider configuration, supported resource types, and schemas. Enterprise accounts only.
secrets-store-api: Cloudflare Secrets Store, for account-level secrets such as API keys and tokens shared across Workers: list and inspect stores, create, list, view, edit, duplicate (keeping the value) and delete secrets singly or in bulk, and check how many secrets the account is using against its quota.
security-insights-api: Cloudflare Security Center insights: list security findings, view full context for large ones, classify as false positive or accepted risk, and dismiss them. Counts by class, severity, type and partner, audit history, on-demand scans with quota, account scan settings, and partner (RiskRecon) integration settings and discovered shadow hosts and zones.
security-txt-api: Cloudflare security.txt for a zone: view, create or update, and delete the file served at /.well-known/security.txt, which tells security researchers how to report vulnerabilities (contact details and disclosure policy).
signed-url-api: Cloudflare signed URLs, with a single internal route for testing signed URLs. It does not create, sign, or manage URLs or keys, so open it only when you need to test signed URL behavior.
smart-shield-api: Cloudflare Smart Shield: view and change a zone's Smart Shield settings, create, list, inspect, update, patch and delete health checks that monitor origin servers, and clear the Cache Reserve (it must be disabled first, takes up to 24 hours, can't be undone) and check clearing progress.
snippets-api: Cloudflare Snippets, small pieces of JavaScript that run on requests to a zone: list, view, create, update and delete snippets, read a snippet's code, and manage the zone's snippet rules (list, replace, or delete all) that control which requests trigger each snippet.
spectrum-api: Cloudflare Spectrum, which proxies TCP/UDP traffic for non-HTTP applications: create, view, list, update and delete Spectrum applications for a zone's origin, list available protocols, and pull analytics such as current-minute usage, metrics by time interval, summaries, and bandwidth by zone.
speed-api: Cloudflare Observatory (Speed) for website performance testing: run page speed tests from a chosen region, view test results and history, list tested pages, see Core Web Vitals trends over time, create, view and delete recurring scheduled tests, delete a page's tests, and check test quota by plan.
sql-api: Cloudflare Analytics SQL API: run SQL queries against analytics datasets, with optional parameters, time range, and account or zone scope, and output as JSON or tab-separated text. Also browse the dataset catalogue, including column names and types and attributes found in an account's own data.
ssl-certificate-packs: Cloudflare SSL/TLS certificate packs for a zone: list and inspect active packs, order advanced certificate packs, delete them, check certificate pack quota, restart validation for a pack that timed out, and add Cloudflare branding to a pack.
ssl-client-certificates: Cloudflare API Shield mTLS client certificates for a zone: create a client certificate, list them by status with pagination, view details of one, revoke a certificate (it goes to pending revocation first), and reactivate one that is still pending revocation.
ssl-core: Cloudflare SSL/TLS core settings for a zone: analyze a certificate's hostnames, algorithm and expiry; Universal SSL settings; certificate validation status and method; DCV delegation; CA hostname associations; Certificate Transparency email alerts; automatic SSL/TLS mode upgrader; and automatic origin TLS key-exchange selection.
ssl-custom-certificates: Cloudflare custom SSL certificates for a zone: upload your own certificate and private key, list, search and filter certificates, view details (bundle method, geographic restrictions, keyless server), replace the certificate or key, delete certificates, and set priority order when several overlap.
ssl-keyless-certificates: Cloudflare Keyless SSL, which lets Cloudflare terminate TLS while private keys stay on your own key server: create a keyless configuration for a zone, list them, view one, change its name, host or port, and delete it.
ssl-mtls-certificates: Cloudflare mTLS certificates you bring yourself (BYO-CA): upload a certificate for mTLS-enabled services, list and inspect uploaded certificates, see which Cloudflare services a certificate is associated with, and delete one that is not in use. Certificates from Cloudflare's managed CA are handled elsewhere.
ssl-origin-ca-certificates: Cloudflare Origin CA certificates, which secure the connection between Cloudflare and your origin server: create a certificate, list the certificates for a zone, look one up by serial number, and revoke one.
ssl-origin-tls-client-auth: Cloudflare authenticated origin pulls (origin mTLS), where Cloudflare presents a client certificate to your origin: upload, list, inspect and delete zone-level or per-hostname client certificates, turn zone-level authentication on or off, and associate hostnames with certificates, enabling, disabling or invalidating each one.
stream-core: Cloudflare Stream account basics: check storage use and billable minutes viewed over time, create, list and delete signing keys (deleting revokes signed URLs), and set up, view or remove the webhook that notifies you about on-demand video uploads.
stream-live-inputs: Cloudflare Stream live inputs: create, list, inspect, update and delete live inputs that receive broadcasts, and get their streaming credentials. Disable or re-enable a live input, rotate its keys, and manage outputs that simulcast or restream to other RTMP or SRT destinations.
stream-videos: Cloudflare Stream videos: upload by TUS, from a URL, or through a direct upload link for end-users; list, inspect, edit, clip and delete videos; extra audio tracks; captions and subtitles per language (upload, AI-generate, fetch WebVTT, delete); downloadable copies; signed URL tokens; and legacy embed HTML.
stream-watermarks: Cloudflare Stream watermark profiles: create a watermark profile by uploading an image, list all profiles on the account, view the details of one profile, and delete a profile. Profiles hold the overlay image settings that are applied to videos.
tags-api: Cloudflare resource tags: view, set, replace or remove the tags on a specific account or zone-level resource, list all tagged resources in an account, and see which tag keys and values are in use, including the values for a given key, optionally filtered by resource type.
tenant-custom-nameservers-api: Cloudflare tenant custom nameservers: add a custom nameserver to a tenant account, list the custom nameservers a tenant has, and delete one. Use it to manage vanity (branded) nameservers for a tenant's DNS zones.
tunnel-api: Cloudflare Tunnel: list the tunnels in an account and filter the results, for example to find a tunnel by name or check its status. This group only lists tunnels; it does not create, configure, or delete them.
tunnels-api: Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared): create, list, rename, and delete tunnels, and edit the ingress rules and origin settings of remotely managed ones. Also fetch the token that runs cloudflared, create short-lived management tokens (e.g. for log streaming), and inspect or clean up connectors and connections, such as after rotating tokens.
url-normalization-api: Cloudflare URL Normalization settings for a zone: view the current configuration, update it, or delete it to restore defaults. This controls how incoming request URLs are normalized (for example, cleaning up path formatting) before they reach rules and your origin.
url-scanner-api: Cloudflare URL Scanner: submit one URL or a batch to scan, then fetch a scan's results by ID. Retrieve its screenshot (desktop, mobile or tablet), rendered DOM, HAR network log, and raw responses for individual requests. Search past scans by domain, ASN, resource path or hash, verdict, date, or API key.
user-core: Cloudflare user profile: view and edit your own user details and account memberships, review audit logs of changes (filter by actor, zone, or time range), list, inspect, and accept or decline account invitations, manage your subscriptions (view, update, delete), and list load balancing origin health change events.
user-firewall: Cloudflare user-level IP Access rules, which apply to all zones owned by the current user: create rules to block, challenge or allow an IP, range, country or ASN, list and filter rules, view one rule, change its action or notes, and delete it.
user-load-balancers: Cloudflare Load Balancing at the user level: create, edit and delete health monitors and origin pools (single or bulk edits), check pool health, preview monitor and pool health results, see which resources reference a monitor or pool, and list region mappings.
user-memberships: Cloudflare user account memberships: list the accounts the signed-in user belongs to, view the details of a single membership, accept or reject a pending account invitation, and leave an account by removing the user's own membership.
user-tokens: Cloudflare user API tokens: create, list, inspect, update and delete the access tokens you own, including expired ones. Roll a token's secret, verify that a token works, and look up the available permission groups to choose which permissions a token gets.
vectorize-api: Cloudflare Vectorize vector database: create, list, inspect and delete indexes; insert or upsert vectors; fetch, list and delete vectors by ID; run nearest-neighbor similarity queries; and manage metadata indexes (up to 10 properties) that enable filtering queries by metadata.
waiting-rooms-core: Cloudflare Waiting Room core: create, list, view, update, edit and delete waiting rooms that queue visitors when a site is busy, check a room's current status, preview a custom waiting room page before using it, and read or change zone-level Waiting Room settings.
waiting-rooms-events: Cloudflare Waiting Room events (Advanced subscription only): create, list, view, update, patch and delete scheduled events that temporarily change a waiting room's behavior for a set time window, such as a sale or launch. Also previews an event's settings as if active, including values inherited from the room. Events cannot overlap.
waiting-rooms-rules: Cloudflare Waiting Room rules: list the rules on a waiting room, create a rule, edit or delete a single rule, or replace the whole rule set at once. Rules decide which requests bypass the queue or are held in it. Creating and replacing rules requires the Waiting Room Advanced subscription.
web-assets-discovery: Cloudflare web asset discovery: list the web and API operations (endpoints) found from a zone's traffic, look up one by discovery ID, update the state of one or several (for example, review or ignore them), and export the discovered API operations as OpenAPI schemas.
web-assets-labels: Cloudflare web and API asset labels for a zone: list managed and user-defined labels, view a label with its attached operations, create, edit, replace and delete user-defined labels (singly or in bulk), and replace the set of web and API operations attached to a managed or user-defined label.
web-assets-operations: Cloudflare web assets endpoint management for a zone: create, list, inspect and delete web or API operations (host, method, path), singly or in bulk. Also attach, remove or replace labels on operations, singly or in bulk, and export tracked operations as OpenAPI schemas.
web3-api: Cloudflare Web3 gateways: create, list, inspect, edit and delete Web3 hostnames (IPFS and Ethereum gateways), and manage the IPFS Universal Path Gateway content list, including viewing or updating the list and adding, editing, listing and removing its entries (for example blocked content).
workers-builds-api: Workers Builds Previews for a Worker: list and inspect Previews, edit the tracked branch, automation flags and build settings, trigger a build for a Preview, list a Preview's build history, and migrate a legacy non-production build trigger to Previews.
workers-for-platforms-dispatch-namespace: Cloudflare Workers for Platforms dispatch namespaces: create, list, edit and delete namespaces, and manage the customer scripts inside them. Upload, fetch, replace and delete scripts (singly or in bulk by tag), upload static assets, view bindings and settings, edit settings, manage secrets, and tag scripts.
workers-vpc-api: Workers VPC connectivity services: create, list, inspect, update and delete the services that let Cloudflare Workers reach private resources, such as internal hosts and APIs, outside the public internet. Each service is managed by its ID within the account.
workflows-api: Cloudflare Workflows, durable multi-step jobs: list, inspect and delete workflows; start single or batch instances; pause, resume, restart or terminate them; send events to running instances; read instance logs, status and full step output; view workflow versions and graphs; manage concurrency keys that limit parallel steps; account settings such as instance retention.
zaraz-api: Cloudflare Zaraz, third-party tool manager for a zone: read and update the Zaraz configuration, get the default configuration, export the full published configuration with secret variables, publish the preview configuration, list and inspect past published versions and restore one, and get or change the workflow setting.
zero-trust-access: Cloudflare Zero Trust Access: manage protected applications and their policies (app-specific and reusable, policy tests, user checks, token revocation), Access groups, service tokens, mTLS certificates, short-lived certificates, SSH CA and infrastructure targets, custom pages, SAML encryption certificates, signing keys, tags, users and sessions, SCIM user populations, MFA authenticators, and audit, JIT and SCIM logs.
zero-trust-casb: Cloudflare CASB (SaaS security posture): connect, pause, resume and edit SaaS integrations and see supported apps and auth methods; review security findings and instances (ignore, archive, tune severity); manage custom finding types; DLP content findings; automated policies; remediation jobs; webhooks; CSV exports.
zero-trust-core: Cloudflare Zero Trust account-level settings and user management: view and change account connectivity settings, remove a user from an Access or Gateway seat, and delete a user's MFA authenticators, including passkeys, PIV keys and FIDO2 keys, to revoke their enrollment.
zero-trust-cws: Cloudflare Zero Trust CWS (cloud workload security) policy management: create and manage deployments, Rego policies and policy sets, reusable workload selectors, domain access control lists, basic-auth credentials and their password secrets, Rego library modules and metadata documents, and tenant structures with batch node hierarchy edits.
zero-trust-devices: Cloudflare Zero Trust WARP devices: list, inspect, update and delete devices and registrations, device settings profiles (default and custom), managed networks, device IP profiles, posture rules and integrations, WARP client version deployment groups, uninstall and admin override codes, and the global emergency disconnect switch.
zero-trust-dex: Cloudflare Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) for WARP devices: list devices and their live or historical status, create and manage synthetic HTTP and traceroute tests and rules, view test results, percentiles, network paths and ISPs, colo usage, WARP change events, and run remote device commands with quota and artifact downloads.
zero-trust-dlp: Cloudflare Zero Trust Data Loss Prevention: manage DLP profiles (custom and predefined) and detection entries, datasets (word lists, EDM), document fingerprints, and regex validation. Also covers custom prompt topics, data classes, data tags, sensitivity groups and levels, email scanning rules and provider mapping, proximity-word and Worker validators, account settings, and usage limits.
zero-trust-gateway: Cloudflare Zero Trust Gateway: create and manage filtering rules (including MSP parent-account rules and expiration reset), lists of domains/IPs/URLs, locations, proxy endpoints, PAC files, and TLS inspection certificates. Also covers account settings (antivirus, block page, logging), app and category lookups, DNS destination IPs, and Zero Trust account setup.
zero-trust-identity-providers: Cloudflare Zero Trust identity providers for Access login: add, view, update and delete identity providers, manage IdP federation grants, create SAML encryption certificates, and view or delete users and groups synced from the identity provider through SCIM provisioning.
zero-trust-organization: Cloudflare Zero Trust organization: create the organization for an account or zone, and read or update its configuration. Also manages the organization's DNS over HTTPS (DoH) settings and its trust settings, which can be read, updated, replaced, or reset.
zero-trust-risk-scoring: Cloudflare Zero Trust user risk scoring: view and update the behaviors and weights that raise a user's risk score, get an account-wide risk summary or one user's score breakdown, reset a user's score, and manage integrations that feed in external risk signals (create, list, get by ID or reference ID, update, delete).
zones-core: Cloudflare zones (domains): create, list, search, get, edit and delete zones, re-check activation of pending zones, and view available plans and rate plans. Also reads and changes zone settings: Aegis dedicated egress IPs, APO for WordPress, Binary AST, Fonts, HTTP/2 prioritization, origin HTTP version and H2 streams, RUM, Speed Brain, and image and media transformations (allowed origins, C2PA).
zones-holds: Cloudflare zone holds: place a hold on a zone so no other account can create or activate a zone with the same hostname, optionally covering subdomains. Check whether a hold exists and its details, change the hold-after time or subdomain setting, and release a hold permanently or temporarily.
zones-hostnames: Cloudflare per-hostname TLS settings within a zone: list the TLS setting for all hostnames, get it for a single hostname, update the value for a hostname, or delete a hostname's override.
zones-origin-tls-compliance-modes: Cloudflare Origin TLS Compliance Modes for a zone: view, set, replace, or clear the compliance modes (fips, pqh) that limit which TLS key-exchange algorithms Cloudflare uses when connecting to the origin server. Multiple modes combine as an intersection; an empty list or deleting the setting removes the constraint.
zones-subscriptions: Cloudflare zone subscriptions, the billing plan and add-ons attached to a single zone (domain). Look up a zone's current subscription details, create a subscription, change the plan or add-ons, and delete a zone's subscription.
